ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as consolidated; transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849, Directive (EU) 2018/843 and Regulation (EU) 2023/1113); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), supplemented by Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 January 2019; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (SARL provisions); Law of 19 December 2002 on the trade and companies register and annual accounts; CSSF global AML/CFT framework and CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 for covered entities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies), as amended by the Law of 19 May 2023 on the modernisation of the SARL (in force 1 September 2023); SARL regime at Articles 710-1 to 710-15; registration and publication governed by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), Articles 1-36.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg; electronic filing exclusively via the e-RCS portal at www.lbr.lu / rcs.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Articles of Incorporation/Statutes) executed either before a Luxembourg civil-law notary or, since the Law of 19 May 2023, by private written deed (sous seing privé) signed by all shareholders; filed electronically with the RCS together with the registration form (formulaire d'inscription) and the signed declaration of conformity (déclaration de conformité).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for SARLs since the Law of 19 May 2023 (in force 1 September 2023); the capital is freely set in the articles of incorporation (practically EUR 1 or more; cross-border BPO entities commonly adopt EUR 12,000). All subscribed cash contributions must be fully paid up at incorporation and, under standard banking practice, are deposited in a blocked (escrow) account opened in the name of the company 'in formation' with a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution; the bank's blocked-capital attestation is filed with the RCS and the funds are released to the company only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION

[•] SARL (the 'Company'), adopted unanimously by the founding managers on [date].

RESOLVED:
1. The articles of incorporation are ratified and all formation expenses approved.
2. The share capital of EUR [•], divided into [•] shares, is confirmed fully subscribed and paid up.
3. The registered office is fixed at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
4. [Name(s)] are appointed as manager(s), each authorised to act singly.
5. The manager(s) are authorised to open bank accounts, release the blocked capital upon RCS registration, and complete all filings with the Luxembourg Business Registers and RESA publication.
6. All ancillary documents may be executed by any one manager.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and excise duties. Principal portals: impotsdirects.public.lu, ecdf.etat.lu, guichet.lu, and lbr.lu for RCS filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg-resident SARL is constituted by notarial deed filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu). RCS registration automatically creates the ACD tax file and the 13-digit national identification number (matricule), which is the corporate TIN for direct taxes. The AEDT automatically assigns a separate VAT identification number formatted as LU + 8 digits. Non-established foreign suppliers not requiring incorporation must file direct VAT registration with the AEDT via the eCDF portal and receive a LU VAT ID without a Luxembourg registered office, unless supplies are reverse-charged to a Luxembourg VAT-registered customer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists; a SARL is mandatorily an opaque resident company. Available statutory elections: (i) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) for closely linked persons with AEDT authorization; (ii) Luxembourg fiscal unity (intégration fiscale, Article 164bis LIR) for a resident parent directly or indirectly holding at least 95% of the subsidiary, subject to ACD approval; (iii) the IP box regime (80% exemption of qualifying IP income, Article 50ter LIR) if the specific substance conditions are met; and (iv) documentation-driven arm's-length adjustments for ATAD hybrid mismatch rules, which otherwise apply automatically without election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Luxembourg-established SARL: registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply unless the small-business exemption applies for annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 (excl. VAT). Non-established suppliers have no de minimis threshold for domestic B2C supplies made outside the OSS/IOSS schemes; intra-Union distance sales and qualifying e-services to non-taxable consumers exceed the EUR 10,000 EU-wide annual threshold before OSS registration is required. B2B services supplied to a Luxembourg VAT-registered customer are reverse-charged, so a non-established seller generally need not register for those supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no mandatory B2B e-invoicing, no real-time fiscal clearance, and no digital stamping/API pre-clearance regime as of 2025. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory in PEPPOL/UBL format for invoices issued under public procurement contracts. All tax invoices must contain the mandatory fields of Article 226 of EU Directive 2006/112/EC. For 2025, the standard VAT rate is temporarily 18% with reduced rates of 15%, 9%, and 4%; these revert to 17%, 14%, 8%, and 3% from 1 January 2026.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Inbound helpdesk and outbound tele-sales BPO services supplied to a non-EU business customer are deemed supplied at the customer's place of establishment (Article 44 EU VAT Directive, Article 13 of the Luxembourg VAT Law). The supply is therefore outside Luxembourg territorial VAT and gives rise to a full input VAT deduction, producing an effective zero rating. Eligibility requires contractual and documentary evidence that the recipient is a taxable person established outside the EU and that the service is actually performed for that recipient. For physical goods, the 0% export exemption requires the goods to leave the EU within 3 months of supply and proof of export to be compiled within 90 days.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed BPO Master Services Agreement and Statement of Work
Non-EU customer tax residence certificate or equivalent VAT/business registration extract
Agent performance logs, call detail records, and service completion reports
Commercial invoice and foreign exchange receipt evidence (SWIFT MT103 or bank credit advice)
For ancillary physical exports: customs export declaration, bill of lading or airway bill, and inward remittance certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reopen up to five prior VAT years and reassess any unjustified zero-rated export at the applicable standard rate (18% in 2025) on the gross invoice amount, with input VAT clawed back and late interest accruing at 0.6% per month. Incomplete or contradictory export files are treated as documentation defects and may attract administrative penalties; deliberate misdeclaration or fraudulent documentation can lead to penalties of 50% or more of the tax evaded, criminal fines up to EUR 100,000, and imprisonment. Directors and officers may be held jointly liable where Luxembourg unlawful-act liability rules apply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national monetary authority, operator of TARGET2 liquidity settlement and collector of balance-of-payments statistics; banking prudential supervision and AML/KYC enforcement lie with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF). Currency policy is governed by Eurosystem rules (TFEU Art. 63) and Council Directive 88/361/EEC; no Luxembourg-specific exchange-control authority imposes convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility. Luxembourg is a Euro-area member and applies zero exchange controls on the EUR; both trade payments and capital movements are free. Profit remittance requires no prior authorization: annual accounts must be approved, the net-asset test under the law of 10 August 1915 must be met, and a 15% domestic dividend withholding tax must be declared (treaty-reduced where applicable). Invoicing in USD, INR or PHP is unrestricted; foreign-currency balances may be retained indefinitely and conversion to EUR is freely executable at market rates. The servicing bank reports cross-border flows to the BCL for statistical purposes only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or mandatory conversion regime exists. A Luxembourg SARL may retain 100% of foreign-currency export and service proceeds in the original currency in domestic or foreign accounts; there is no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio. The only obligation is statistical: cross-border payments are reported to the BCL by the servicing credit institution under BCL reporting regulations, requiring no action by the company itself.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium for ancillary treasury use; Low as primary banking solution. Wise B2B and comparable EU-authorized EMIs/payment institutions (e.g., Revolut Payments, solaris and other PSD2-passported firms) are accepted for small-ticket cross-border disbursements to BPO subcontractors (INR, PHP, USD) and for fast collections from foreign clients. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI is not a credit institution and may not hold the statutory SARL share-capital blockage; (ii) funds on an e-money account are safeguarded but are NOT covered by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme (FGDL); (iii) the EMI account is not eligible for Commercial LC, TARGET2 or cash-management sweeps; (iv) the main operating ledger, RBE/KYC nexus and statutory audit trail must remain at a fully licensed bank. Recommended policy: cap Wise/EMI settlement at 10% of monthly treasury volume and cascade all balances monthly to the principal EUR account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory in-person Board presence is not required for bank onboarding. Remote video-KYC is permitted for low-risk entities under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and CSSF guidance when identification meets equivalent-reliability standards (LuxTrust/NID for EU residents). Practical mandate: EU-resident directors and managers can complete fully remote opening with video identity check plus electronic signature; non-EU directors/UBOs must provide notarized and apostilled passport copies (or consular certification), and most Tier-1 banks require at least one compliance interview (secure video-call) as well as a notarized power-of-attorney executed before a Luxembourg notary for local signatory rights. A physical visit of the UBO to Luxembourg is usually waived for a Low_Risk_Standard BPO SARL provided local substance (lease, payroll, Luxembourg manager or gérant) is evidenced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Luxembourg-registered SARL without employees or local management (letterbox risk versus BPO substance claim)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office lease in the company name (not pure domiciliation); Luxembourg payroll evidence or outstaffing agreement; local IT/telecom infrastructure (EU-hosted PBX or cloud contact-center); minutes of gérant meetings showing decisions taken in Luxembourg; copies of Luxembourg social-security (CCSS) registrations of local staff; annual business plan and signed client contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket card-not-present inflows from tele-sales with elevated refund or chargeback patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS v4.0 attestation; merchant acquiring agreement with the payment processor; documented refund and complaint-handling policy; monthly chargeback statistics and reconciliation pack; call-log and CRM records evidencing genuine call-center activity; declaration of transaction-monitoring controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the offshore-centric beneficial-ownership chain (trusts or multi-jurisdiction holding layers)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing confirmation; corporate-tree schematic down to ultimate individuals; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations signed by each UBO; 12 months of originator bank statements; certified copies of trust deeds or holding constitutional documents; audited financial statements of the parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursements to unlicensed subcontractors in high-risk jurisdictions (South Asia, North Africa call-center capacity)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYC vendor file per subcontractor: business registration, AML and sanctions screening results, anti-money-laundering questionnaire, bank details and license of its bank; signed master service agreement with fixed-price schedule and audit clause; dual-signatory payment approval; quarterly payment-versus-invoice reconciliation statements; cap on new beneficiaries with monthly compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement instructions routed via unregulated PSPs or crypto-linked accounts (anomalous round-tripping)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution prohibiting crypto-denominated settlement; policy requiring all inbound and outbound payments to be settled exclusively through EU-licensed credit institutions or PSD2-authorized EMIs; list of approved PSPs; reconciliation of payment-provider statements with bank receipts; audit trail of every MT103 and SEPA batch.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The SARL incorporation capital (statutory minimum EUR 12,000 subscribed; at least EUR 2,000 paid-up before notarization) is deposited, prior to the notary deed, either with the Luxembourg notary or - preferred in banking practice - on a blocked account ('compte bloqué') opened in the name of the 'SARL en formation'. Routing protocol: SEPA credit transfer (EUR) or SWIFT MT103 from the UBO's account to the blocked account; the remittance information field must carry purpose code EQUI (equity investment) and the notary file reference together with the corporate name; the bank then issues the capital-release confirmation to the notary upon registration with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés. No exchange-control authorization is required for the inbound injection; the bank records the transaction for BCL balance-of-payments statistics. Subsequent paid-in capital increases follow the same routing with reference to the notarial deed of increase.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary settlement: SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) for EU/EEA vendors and payroll; SEPA Instant for urgent operational top-ups; TARGET2/T2 large-value credit transfer for EUR items above EUR 1 million; SWIFT MT103 (STP) for non-EEA subcontractors (India, Philippines, Morocco, Tunisia) with mandatory beneficiary information and remittance reference to commercial invoices. Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) are available but commercially impractical for BPO service flows - they should be reserved for hardware or telecom equipment purchases; service subcontracts use open-account terms with dual-signatory approval and monthly reconciliation. Wise B2B can be layered as a fast low-value rail for INR/PHP subcontractor payments, with weekly cascade to the principal bank so the statutory ledger remains complete.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/NOK) with tenors up to 12 months under a bank FX Master Agreement (IFEMA/ICOM or ISDA terms)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on INR and PHP for hedging subcontractor cost exposure where onshore deliverability is unavailable
FX swaps for temporary conversion of USD receipts into EUR disbursement liquidity without ending the currency position
Outright vanilla FX options (puts/calls) up to 12 months, subject to collateral or credit-line requirements

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) only if acquisition or working-capital debt is drawn (otherwise unnecessary for the BPO treasury model); all OTC derivatives are subject to EMIR trade reporting and, where applicable, clearing and margining thresholds, as well as CSSF/BCL prudential rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) filing with the Register of Commerce and Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the shareholders' general meeting within 6 months of the financial year-end; RCS filing within 1 month of approval and no later than 7 months after the balance sheet date (e.g., for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: District court may impose a periodic penalty (up to EUR 500 per day) and fines under the RCS regime; persistent non-filing exposes the company to administrative strike-off from the RCS and loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once every calendar year within the month following the anniversary date of the initial RBE registration or the last annual confirmation; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per infringement for individuals and up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal persons; wilful non-compliance is a criminal offence and may be published.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax return (Form 500) together with settlement of any corporate tax liabilities, including the minimum net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing and payment due by 31 May following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; a filing extension to 31 December may be granted upon written request to the ACD.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.8% per month; default surcharge ranging from 10% to 50% of the assessed tax; potential criminal fines for deliberate omissions; enforced recovery procedures against assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is mandatory if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total assets exceeding EUR 4.4 million; net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million; average number of employees exceeding 25. Where these thresholds are exceeded, a Luxembourg-approved réviseur d'entreprises must be appointed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 (transposing the EU Accounting Directive); IFRS is permitted on a voluntary basis and is mandatory for consolidated financial statements of certain groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file a confirmation statement through the Luxembourg Business Registers online portal within one month of the anniversary of its RBE registration or of its last annual confirmation, certifying the accuracy of the registered beneficial-owner data. Any transfer of shares or adjustment in the underlying control chain must be separately filed within 30 days; the annual confirmation is free of charge and resets the one-year confirmation cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Management Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 – USD 3,500 per annum for a standard Luxembourg corporate service agent providing registered office and filing coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 10,000 per annum when the SARL exceeds the statutory audit thresholds; zero when audit-exempt

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate combined top rate in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT, yielding 18.19%, plus 6.75% municipal business tax); the standalone CIT marginal rate is 17% on taxable income above EUR 175,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. Luxembourg grants an IP Box exemption equal to 80% of qualifying intellectual property net income, an investment tax credit for eligible new assets, and a participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains. The BPO call-center fee income is taxable at the ordinary aggregate rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed through the MyGuichet business e-Space electronic portal of the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year accounting period, the Form 210 return is due no later than 31 December of the following year; the assessment office may set an earlier due date on the pre-printed form. A justified extension may be requested for non-calendar-year financial periods.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer registration details: entity name, RCS number, registered office, directors and representatives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident permanent establishments must identify the Luxembourg PE address and appointed tax representative; a fully resident Luxembourg SARL uses its registered office details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial accounting profit or loss before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident operates only through a Luxembourg PE, the accounting profit must be re-attributed to the PE applying the OECD Article 7 separate-enterprise principle. Remote back-office activity without a fixed place of business in Luxembourg creates no Luxembourg filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible charges, disallowed provisions, hidden profit distributions and reversal of hidden reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically connected to the Luxembourg PE are deductible; head-office and intra-group charges must be arm's length and fully documented.
Non-residents enter only Luxembourg-source PE taxable income; treaty protection under the PE Article must be claimed and substantiated with a tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of tax losses carried forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be attributable to the same Luxembourg PE operation; carry-forward is restricted to 17 years and anti-abuse ownership tests may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax at 17%, solidarity surcharge at 7% and municipal business tax at the communal rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax apply only to Luxembourg PE profits allocated to the relevant commune.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing can trigger default tax assessment on an estimated basis, late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, administrative fines for non-compliance, and, in fraudulent cases, criminal tax-evasion penalties of up to EUR 100,000 in fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years for the responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; 0% applies where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or Luxembourg participation-exemption conditions are met, generally requiring a holding of at least 10% for 12 uninterrupted months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA zero or reduced dividend rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must file a current tax residence certificate (TRC), equivalent EU residence certificate or Form 616, together with a beneficial ownership and holding-period statement, with the Luxembourg paying company and, where applicable, the Direct Tax Administration. The reduced rate is applied at source once the ACD approves the withholding relief application; excess withheld tax is recoverable by refund claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Luxembourg law imposes 0% withholding tax on cross-border interest and royalties. Treaty rates are commonly 0% for beneficial owners; no Luxembourg source tax arises except for profit-participating debt instruments or arrangements recast as distributions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No separate Luxembourg statutory Local File or Master File filing threshold exists. Mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting begins for groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million. For all related-party transactions, including centralized call-center service fees, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be available on request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations; instead, Article 56 LIR and the EU ATAD anti-abuse rules require genuine economic substance in Luxembourg. A remote BPO SARL must maintain local employees, physical facilities, operational management and real decision-making; otherwise profits may be reallocated and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of call-center billings, fabrication of outsourcing costs to low-tax affiliates, destruction of wire-transfer records or concealment of foreign bank receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution with fines up to EUR 100,000 (or higher for aggravated fraud) and imprisonment up to 5 years; administrative recapture of evaded tax with late-payment interest and default penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false Form 210 returns or participate in fraudulent invoicing may be personally prosecuted. The corporate veil may be pierced for civil restitution of taxes and social debts; travel bans, asset freezes and imprisonment may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox for BPO profits actually generated by foreign employees, with no local office, no Luxembourg-based staff and no real board control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Luxembourg tax residence and treaty benefits, reallocation of all taxable profits to the actual place of management, disallowance of intercompany deductions and application of Luxembourg GAAR/ATAD sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and managing directors may be jointly and severally liable for reassessed corporate income tax, municipal business tax and withholding taxes; courts may issue director disqualification, travel bans and civil restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Permanent Establishment Mismatch
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a taxable fixed establishment in Luxembourg while billing the services from an offshore affiliate, or compensating the Luxembourg SARL with no arm's length margin over successive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward transfer pricing adjustment, reclassification of the shortfall as deemed dividend subject to 15% withholding tax, late-payment interest and penalties on the additional assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for underserved transfer pricing may be held personally liable if the company becomes insolvent; failure to collect or remit withholding tax is separately sanctionable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership and Compliance Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-volume Wise B2B or wire-transfer client receipts without maintaining the beneficial ownership register, failing to prepare annual accounts, using personal accounts for business receipts, or neglecting KYC checks on subcontractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML fines of up to EUR 500,000 for entities, deregistration from the RCS, freezing of bank accounts and separate administrative penalties for UBO register non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and compliance officers may be personally fined, banned from company management, and criminally prosecuted for wilful failure to report suspicious transfers; civil confiscation of diverted funds may be ordered.
